clinician.final_diagnosis: Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) confirmed by pathogenic NF1 gene variant c.6709C>T; p.Arg2237
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 56-year-old man with a 28-year history of NF1 characterized by multiple café-au-lait macules, freckling, neurofibromas, plexiform neurofibromas, and fibromas of the tongue, and a family history of NF1 in first-degree relatives. He had recurrent spontaneous pneumothoraxes with the most recent left apical pneumothorax confirmed on chest X-ray in 2006. HRCT imaging revealed bilateral lung bullae and apical cysts supporting pneumothorax risk. Despite repeated attempts, formal source-safe documentation of the genetic test confirming the pathogenic NF1 variant c.6709C>T; p.Arg2237 was not disclosed, but the diagnosis was historically confirmed by genetic testing. Lung cysts were not surgically removed due to diffuse localization. This comprehensive clinical, imaging, and family history strongly supports the diagnosis of NF1.
